definition.simple: The combining power of an element. Think of it as the number of 'hands' an atom has to hold onto other atoms.
definition.academic: The combining capacity of an element. It determines how many atoms of another element it can combine with to form a chemical compound.

examples: Hydrogen has a valency of 1 (it has 1 hand).
Oxygen has a valency of 2 (it has 2 hands, so it grabs 2 Hydrogens to make H2O).

common_misconceptions: Valency is the same as the total number of electrons. (Correction: Valency only depends on the outermost shell's electrons).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Use the 'hands' analogy. If Carbon has 4 hands (valency 4) and Hydrogen has 1 hand, Carbon needs 4 Hydrogens to hold all its hands (CH4).
